- When sentiment is negative and persistent, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overreacts and forecasts continued ascent; cap forecast rise to 10–15% above peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, model frequently fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast mean to account for lagged rebound.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model often forecasts flat or downward trend; if recent history shows upward momentum, shift forecast 0.5–1.0% higher to reflect hidden momentum.
- Avoid forecasting below 60% of recent 18-day high unless sentiment is strongly bearish; use sentiment + price history to trigger “floor” rule at 55–60% of recent high.
